open-vale-and-soul-debt.name: Open Vale & Soul-Debt
open-vale-and-soul-debt.conclusion: The ward ritual's threats used to be people; the ward's beauty has a human cost.
open-vale-and-soul-debt.why: Gives Act Five weight without turning the hidden soul-economy seed into exposition.

clues.name: Market Correction
clues.show: As the ritual strains, the vale itself answers — the ground gives up more figures, rising in waves, as if the site is rebalancing a ledger.
clues.points_to: an environmental Fear move — the ritual site spawns more skeletons under pressure. Mechanically central to Act 5.

clues.name: Glass-Bright Ward Sand
clues.show: Where the ward settles, the ground is left strewn with bright glittering sand — lovely, and just a little too sharp to touch.
clues.points_to: the ward's magic has a residue and a cost; beauty with an edge.

clues.name: Legacy Security Badge
clues.show: A broken badge on a fallen figure, naming a security unit that no longer exists — a job title outliving the person.
clues.points_to: the "monster" was an employee; this is a defunct unit, not a boss — people, not enemies.

clues.name: Soul-Audit Memory Shard
clues.show: A cold sliver that, touched, plays a stranger's memory — a name, a debt, a last ordinary afternoon — partial and aching.
clues.points_to: turns abstract "soul-debt" into something the players feel: these were people, audited into assets.

clues.name: Sable Sinecure Secret Caches
clues.show: A forest cache sitting in plain sight, apparently unguarded — which is exactly what makes it terrifying to the locals.
clues.points_to: the Sinecure guards by policy, trap, and fire-falcon consequence, not visible muscle — corporate menace as fine print.

the-ambush-reveal.name: The Ambush Reveal
the-ambush-reveal.conclusion: The overturned cart was staged as an ambush site before the party arrived.
the-ambush-reveal.why: Moves suspicion away from bad luck or a random beast and toward a planned trap.

clues.name: Bramble Strand
clues.show: A length of thorned bramble is wound tight around the wheel-spokes — deliberate, woven, not snagged in passing.
clues.points_to: a thinking hand jammed the wheel; this points past "animal attack."

clues.name: Torn Shipping Seals
clues.show: Broken wax shipping seals are scattered at the cart — and the same torn seals turn up later on Bramble Union gear.
clues.points_to: links the cart to the Bramble — but (hidden seam) the seals are old, suggesting reclaimed goods, not a fresh heist.

clues.name: Route Ledger
clues.show: A water-stained ledger of the driver's route — stops, times, and a final leg that runs straight into trouble.
clues.points_to: the route was known; the cart was targeted, not unlucky.

clues.name: Overturned Wheel Ruts
clues.show: The mud around the cart is gouged in hard, straight scars — the wheels didn't wander off the road, they were dragged and stopped.
clues.points_to: the cart was disabled and positioned, not crashed.

clues.name: Bramble Claim Marker
clues.show: A knotted strand and a pattern of scratch-marks, ordered like a tally or a signature, left where it would be found.
clues.points_to: the ambush was organized and claimed — a system, not a random act.

clues.name: The Wrong Driver
clues.show: The body's livery, hands, and papers don't match this cart. A courier's hands are callused a certain way; these aren't. The name on the manifest isn't the name stitched in the collar.
clues.points_to: the dead "driver" was placed here — wrong person for this run.

clues.name: The Off Provisions
clues.show: The provisions are wrong for the trip — too little water, the wrong rations, food already spoiling that no real courier would have packed.
clues.points_to: nobody actually drove this cart on a real run; it was dressed to look driven.

clues.name: The Too-Neat Wreck
clues.show: For a violent wreck, nothing valuable is actually scattered — the spill is arranged, the "chaos" is tidy, the sealed package conspicuously untouched.
clues.points_to: the scene was set-dressed; a real robbery or beast-kill would look nothing like this.

the-creature-is-innocent.name: The Creature Is Innocent
the-creature-is-innocent.conclusion: The strixwolf did not kill the driver or cause the wreck; it is frightened and scavenging.
the-creature-is-innocent.why: Lets the table choose mercy and see nature contradict the opening propaganda.

clues.name: Tamsin's Wedding Cord
clues.show: A braided cord, soft with wear, knotted around the dead courier's wrist — the kind a person ties for someone they love.
clues.points_to: the victim is Tamsin, a real person with a life — not a loot container; it makes the murder land and the staging crueler.

clues.name: No Predator Wounds
clues.show: The wound that killed the driver is a clean, thin line — not the tear of a beak or the rake of a claw. Whatever did this had an edge, not teeth.
clues.points_to: the death was a blade (the throat was slit) and dressed up as an animal attack.

clues.name: The Wary Flinch
clues.show: The creature watches your every movement and shrinks from it — ears flat, wings tucked, ready to bolt, not to pounce. It is more afraid of you than you are of it.
clues.points_to: it's behaving like prey, not a predator defending a kill.

clues.name: Feeding, Not Hunting
clues.show: It isn't guarding the body at all — it's nosing at droppings and scattered scat near the cargo, scavenging, uninterested in the corpse.
clues.points_to: it came for the Keystone scat / scraps, not to kill; it has no stake in the body.

clues.name: The Late Tracks
clues.show: The creature's prints lie on top of the wheel-ruts and the dragging marks — it arrived after everything else was already done.
clues.points_to: chronology clears it — it showed up post-wreck.

the-bramble-truth.name: The Bramble Truth
the-bramble-truth.conclusion: The Bramble Union are harmed workers and forest defenders, not the simple criminals the propaganda describes.
the-bramble-truth.why: Complicates victory over the Bramble and rewards empathy, capture, or careful interrogation.

clues.name: Reclaimer Personal Effects
clues.show: Among the Bramble fighters' things: a child's toy, half-finished family mending, old contract tags worn smooth — the belongings of people, not raiders.
clues.points_to: these are ordinary, struggling folk; a clean "kill the bandits" victory curdles when you see what they carry.

clues.name: Old Contract Tags
clues.show: The "stolen" seals and tags on the Bramble's goods are old and worn — and many bear the names of the Bramble carrying them.
clues.points_to: their "loot" is their own repossessed wages and goods — they're reclaiming what was taken, not robbing.

clues.name: The Held Blow
clues.show: In the fight, a Bramble fighter has a clean opening — and pulls the strike. A beat of hesitation that doesn't fit a ruthless bandit.
clues.points_to: they don't actually want to kill; the menace is mostly armor.

clues.name: The Interrogation Answer
clues.show: Press a captured Bramble fighter and the bravado cracks: "We used to haul for them. Then the route 'restructured,' and we didn't. The thorns took us in. They don't."
clues.points_to: the Bramble are ex-corporate workers, discarded — the clearest single source of the truth, gated behind capture + RP.

clues.name: The Painted Joy
clues.show: Glimpsed through the thorns: a hidden village painted in bright murals and lit by glowing moss, full of color and care — nothing like the den of thieves you were warned about.
clues.points_to: the Bramble make beauty and community; the "criminal syndicate" framing is propaganda.

the-manufactured-failure.name: The Manufactured Failure
the-manufactured-failure.conclusion: The corporation planned for the ward to fail and monetized the replacement.
the-manufactured-failure.why: Seeds the hidden false-capitalism thesis without stating it to players.

clues.name: Dustless Ward Map
clues.show: An old ward-map furred with dust — except one clean rectangle, where something has been handled, recently and often.
clues.points_to: attention has been focused on one ward/site (where the failure was steered).

clues.name: Relay Tremor Notation
clues.show: A small marginal notation — a tremor reading — showing the wider relay network is already shaking, before anyone here has words for the problem.
clues.points_to: the failure isn't local; the whole system is destabilizing (the sequel seam).

clues.name: Corporate Seal Wax Residue
clues.show: Cold flecks of seal-wax, pressed and re-pressed, where some clerk has filed and re-filed the same patch of reality until it complied.
clues.points_to: a system that documents events into the shape it needs — paperwork overwriting truth.

clues.name: Public-Private Ward Compact
clues.show: A concession contract that turns "protecting the village" into overlapping rights to build it, bill it, power it, guard it, finance it, and narrate it.
clues.points_to: protection has been financialized — the same hand owns the threat, the defense, and the story about both.

clues.name: Route Assurance Contract™
clues.show: A bland, sunny contract, thick with optimistic language, that promises everything and guarantees nothing — and is, technically, completely truthful.
clues.points_to: the company has pre-written the failure into the fine print; everyone is "technically compliant" while the risk sits on the village.

clues.name: The Pre-Dated Invoice
clues.show: An invoice for "emergency ward replacement," cheerful and itemized — dated before the ward actually failed.
clues.points_to: the bill was prepared in advance; the company knew the failure was coming because it arranged it.

clues.name: The Convenient Renewal
clues.show: The ward "happens" to fail exactly as the village's protection contract comes up for renewal — at a generous new rate.
clues.points_to: the timing is the tell; failure is a sales tool.

hush-hidden-struggle.name: Hush's Hidden Struggle
hush-hidden-struggle.conclusion: Hush's joy is real, but corporations are draining its money, labor, and breathing room; low water can be supporting texture, not the core truth.
hush-hidden-struggle.why: Keeps Hush warm while making the cost of protection concrete.

clues.name: The Ward Subscription
clues.show: The villagers explain, cheerfully, what the ward costs them — a steep, endless fee — and that they've been asked to help defend the village themselves while the new ward-stone is installed.
clues.points_to: Hush pays dearly for protection it's now also expected to provide; the deal is lopsided, and they're too kind to call it.

clues.name: The Cheerful Ledger
clues.show: The village books are kept in a bright, hopeful hand — and every column drains outward: tithes, fees, levies, subscriptions, all flowing to the corporations. Almost nothing stays.
clues.points_to: all of Hush's labor and coin is siphoned away; the smiles sit on top of a grim balance sheet.

clues.name: The Drained Water
clues.show: Hush looks freshly painted and warmly tended, but the little public board is crowded with service fees, late-payment ribbons, and household ledger slips marked again and again in outgoing ink.
clues.points_to: Hush is being drained of coin, labor, and choices by protection fees and corporate services; low water may appear as a symptom, but the clue is economic exhaustion.

clues.name: The Patched Everything
clues.show: Every roof, coat, and cart in Hush is mended, re-mended, and mended again — lovingly, expertly, endlessly. Nothing here is new.
clues.points_to: they can afford nothing new; the joy is threadbare but unbroken.

clues.name: The Tired Smile
clues.show: Mid-laugh, a villager's smile slips for half a second — bone-deep tiredness underneath — and then snaps back, brighter than before.
clues.points_to: the joy is real and so is the exhaustion; they carry both at once.

the-propaganda-itself.name: The Propaganda Itself
the-propaganda-itself.conclusion: The cheerful corporate messaging is evidence because later play contradicts it.
the-propaganda-itself.why: Sets the satire baseline and creates callbacks the players can notice later.

clues.name: The Welcome Broadcast™
clues.show: A bright RuneSpark welcome plays you off: "Congratulations on your Provisional Hire! Sablewood is a Certified Adventure Experience™. Nature is Thrilling, Lucrative, and Almost Entirely Survivable! Your Satisfaction Matters Deeply to Us!"
clues.points_to: sets the official story (nature deadly, company kind) that the journey will quietly dismantle.

clues.name: Nature-Is-Deadly Placard™
clues.show: A roadside sign, cheerful and lurid: "WARNING! Unlicensed Wildlife Ahead! Approved Wildlife Available for Purchase. Do Not Befriend the Forest. The Forest Cannot Be Trusted. The Forest Has Not Signed Anything."
clues.points_to: primes fear of nature — directly contradicted by the scared, harmless creature.

clues.name: Bramble-Are-Criminals Notice™
clues.show: A wanted-style notice, brightly printed: "The Bramble Union: An Unlicensed Syndicate of Anarchists, Thieves, and Unlicensed Persons. Report Sightings. Do Not Listen to Them. Especially Do Not Listen to Them."
clues.points_to: primes the party to see the Bramble as villains — contradicted by The Bramble Truth.
